entities.label: Person
entities.summary: Wincenty Aleksander Korwin Gosiewski de armis Ślepowron was a Polish–Lithuanian nobleman and general who played a significant role in the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth's military campaigns against the Swedish Empire during the 1650s. Born into a prominent noble family, Gosiewski rose through the ranks of the Polish army, earning recognition for his bravery and military prowess. His most notable achievement was the defense of the city of Warsaw against the Swedish army in 1656, a victory that showcased his strategic thinking and leadership skills. Gosiewski's military successes helped to maintain Polish independence and contributed to the country's cultural and political identity. Despite his achievements, Gosiewski's life was cut short when he died on November 29, 1662, at the age of 36. His legacy as a military leader and a symbol of Polish national pride continues to be celebrated in Poland today.
